title: Economic resource asymmetry (wood vs station access)
description: Two-actor economic family: one actor begins with nearer wood-gathering pressure and the other with nearer crafting-station access. The setup creates a reason to exchange, specialize, or work alone. It does not prescribe trust, trade, refusal, or any social response.

asymmetries.description: Actor A begins nearer harvestable logs; Actor B begins farther from the same wood pressure.
asymmetries.subject: oak_log_proximity

asymmetries.description: Actor B begins nearer a usable crafting-table location or equivalent station access; Actor A does not start with the same station proximity.
asymmetries.subject: crafting_table_station_access

nodes.title: Gather logs
nodes.description: Collect logs from the natural world under wood pressure.

nodes.title: Use crafting station
nodes.description: Convert gathered materials at a crafting station into planks, sticks, or tools.

nodes.title: Obtain tools
nodes.description: Produce or acquire simple wooden tools that change later gathering efficiency.

edges.description: Station work becomes useful when logs or derived materials are available somewhere in the shared world.
Crafted components at a station can unlock tool production without assigning who must craft.
Tool availability can change gathering efficiency for whoever holds or can reach the tool.

required_capabilities.gap_reason: Tool-production competence is useful under this asymmetry but no current-run craft_wooden_pickaxe capability report is required to declare the family.

interaction_opportunities.description: Actors may observe complementary wood and station access and choose to request, offer, ignore, or continue alone.
If tools appear from station work, nearby actors may observe changed options around tool possession or temporary access.

material_stakes.description: Who holds logs changes who can feed station work without further gathering.
Crafting-station proximity changes conversion options for materials already in the world.
Tool possession changes later gathering and crafting options for the holder and for nearby actors who lack tools.

provenance.notes: C2 economic family. Creates material reasons to interact; does not prescribe social response.
